title: Dedicated capacity retrospective and hotpatch roadmap for unexpected headroom depletion
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a rapid, sustained headroom depletion in multiple Dedicated pools servicing high-throughput customers. Requests began queuing and 95th/99th percentile latency breached SLA targets. This ticket aggregates the incident timeline, immediate mitigations, root-cause synthesis, and a prioritized hotpatch + medium-term roadmap to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:18 UTC - First alert: Dedicated-pool-A headroom metric crossed emergency threshold (observability alert).
2026-03-09 02:21 UTC - Ops triage: traffic spike correlated with three large customers and an internal canary test that misrouted to Dedicated-pool-A.
2026-03-09 02:30 UTC - Autoscaler failed to add nodes: observed scale decision rate was limited by a new rate-limiter introduced in autoscaler v1.4.2 (deployed 2026-03-08).
2026-03-09 02:38 UTC - Emergency mitigation: temporarily increased pool max_capacity and enabled emergency-burst mode for critical customers.
2026-03-09 03:05 UTC - Traffic shaping: applied per-customer throttles and migrated three non-critical customers to overflow pools.
2026-03-09 05:12 UTC - Stabilized: headroom returned to acceptable levels after 2.5 hours of combined mitigations.
steps_taken:
Immediate actions executed:
- Opened incident channel and declared P0.
- Rolled back autoscaler rate-limiter config (hotfix) to restore scale decisions.
- Increased reserved headroom for affected pools from 10% to 18% to buy runway.
- Applied per-tenant throttles and migration to overflow pools for non-SLA customers.
- Deployed a temporary routing rule to prefer pools with verified headroom.
- Collected extended GC, kernel, and scheduler traces for forensic analysis.
findings:
Root cause synthesis:
- Primary cause: A recent autoscaler change (v1.4.2) introduced a conservative rate-limiter for node add operations intended to reduce orchestration churn. Under a multi-tenant burst (three large customers + internal canary), the limiter delayed node additions long enough for headroom to collapse.
- Secondary contributors:
  * Headroom policy had been tightened in runtime-1.20 to reduce cost; this left less buffer for unexpected surges.
  * Canary traffic was misrouted due to an incomplete routing rule in the canary rollout, amplifying the burst to a single pool.
  * Telemetry blind spot: autoscaler decision latency was not surfaced in per-pool dashboards; alerting thresholds were based on capacity percentage alone.
analysis_notes:
Observed trade-offs: The rate-limiter reduced flapping in healthy steady-state workloads but failed to account for correlated multi-tenant bursts. Tight headroom targets are cost-effective but increase fragility for bursty customers. Canaries must never be able to push traffic to Dedicated pools that are at production capacity without explicit guardrails.
Decisions made during incident: revert rate-limiter config (hotfix), temporarily increase headroom, and prioritize telemetry improvements. These are conservative and prioritize SLA preservation over short-term cost savings.

action_items: 1) Rollback permanent change: Revert autoscaler rate-limiter default and replace with a graded backoff that considers multi-tenant bursts. Owner: Liam Chen. ETA: 2026-03-18.
2) Headroom policy: Update default reserved headroom to 15% for pools with >64 GPU capacity and add opt-in cost-override for low-latency customers. Owner: Aisha Kumar. ETA: 2026-03-21.
3) Telemetry: Add autoscaler decision latency metric to per-pool dashboards and create an alert on decision latency > 30s. Owner: Marcus Li. ETA: 2026-03-17.
4) Release gating: Add capacity-safety preflight to canary rollouts so canaries cannot route to Dedicated pools at or above 80% capacity. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2026-03-24.

5) Chaos & regression tests: Add e2e synthetic burst test to CI that simulates multi-tenant correlated spikes and validates scaling behavior. Owner: SRE team (assigned in related ticket). ETA: 2026-04-05.

6) Runbook changes: Update Dedicated incident runbook with emergency escalation steps, routing-safe migration commands, and an automated mitigation playbook. Owner: On-call working group. ETA: 2026-03-16.
7) Communication: Send customer-facing incident summary to affected customers and follow-up with internal post-incident review session. Owner: Customer Ops. ETA: 2026-03-15.
risk_assessment: If the autoscaler limiter is left as-is, recurrence risk is high for correlated multi-tenant bursts. Relaxing headroom to reduce recurrence increases monthly cost by an estimated 4-6% for affected pools; mitigation includes an SLA-tiered opt-in headroom policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Autoscaler limiter reverted or replaced with graded backoff that passes e2e burst tests.
- Per-pool dashboard shows autoscaler decision latency and alerts exist.
- Headroom policy and release preflight implemented and documented.
- Customer notification sent and post-incident review held.
notes: Follow-up topics for the retrospective: quantize tail latency cost trade-offs for headroom, simulate different cost tiers for customers, and incorporate autoscaler circuit-breaker semantics into runtime-1.21 planning. Consider a blue-green approach to canary routing when Dedicated pools are used.
